---
title: "Stress DSA (Output 3)"
guide-section: "User Guide"
---

Excel analogues: **Input 6**, residual financing in **Input 7**, external B
and public B1 sheets, and Output 3-1 / 3-2. Edit those sheets in Excel, save,
then reload.

> Excel → `load_core` + `load_stress` + `load_rating` → stress suites → Output 3

## Load and compute

```python
from pathlib import Path

from lic_dsf.load import load_core, load_rating, load_stress
from lic_dsf.output import output_31_table, output_32_table
from lic_dsf.stress import (
    run_a1_historical_external,
    run_standard_external_stress,
    run_standard_public_stress,
)

workbook = Path("data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx")
macro, external, ext_base, pub_base = load_core(workbook)
stress = load_stress(workbook)
rating = load_rating(workbook)

external_stress = run_standard_external_stress(
    macro, external, stress.input6, stress.residual
)
public_stress = run_standard_public_stress(
    macro, external, stress.input6, stress.residual
)
historical = run_a1_historical_external(macro, external, stress.residual)

out_3_1 = output_31_table(
    ext_base,
    historical=historical,
    external_stress=external_stress,
    public_stress=public_stress,
    thresholds=rating.ci.thresholds.as_dict(),
)
out_3_2 = output_32_table(
    pub_base,
    public_stress=public_stress,
    public_threshold=rating.ci.thresholds.public_pv_debt_to_gdp,
)
```

The suite functions return dictionaries of scenario ID to stressed book.
Use `stress_external_panel(external_stress["B1_GDP"])` or the public
equivalent to inspect one scenario. Output 2 presents the same stressed ratios;
official workbook chart chrome is outside the Python panel API.

## Tailored and customized stresses

`run_tailored_external_stress` and `run_tailored_public_stress` consume
`stress.tailored` and respect the Input 6 applicability flags. They return A2
and applicable C-test books:

```python
from lic_dsf.stress import run_tailored_external_stress

tailored_external = run_tailored_external_stress(
    macro,
    external,
    stress.residual,
    stress.tailored,
    stress.input6,
)
```

Pass a `CustomizedScenarioSpec` as `custom_spec=` when A2 should use a custom
path. Customized scenarios belong to the stress workflow; the probability
approach on Output 6 is a separate calculation.

## Excel cues

| Concept | Template |
|---------|----------|
| Shock magnitudes and applicability | Input 6 |
| External/public residual-financing terms | Input 7 |
| External stressed ratios | B sheets → Output 3-1 |
| Public stressed ratios | B1 → Output 3-2 |

External DSA residual fill is normally external PPG MLT. Public fill uses the
Input 7 external MLT / domestic MLT / short-term shares.

Public GFN is solved through the fiscal and debt-service identity with a
fixed-point loop. Domestic residual-financing interest uses the baseline GDP
deflator path rather than B1 shocked LCU inflation.

The complete worked example is
[`demo/stress_dsa.ipynb`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/demo/stress_dsa.ipynb).
